Credit sources

Compare Sophia, Study.com, StraighterLine, CLEP, and other credit sources

The best credit source is the one that fills a useful requirement at a workable total cost and pace. Start with the receiving degree, then compare eligible ways to complete each remaining row.

DegreeSteps editorial team6 min readReviewed 2026-11-01

On this page

  1. Use the same questions for every source
  2. Subscription and self-paced course providers
  3. Credit examinations and exam preparation
  4. Look beyond the familiar subscription brands
  5. Include learning you already have
  6. Compare the full course basket

Put this into a plan.

Build my degree path →

Use the same questions for every source

Ask which exact requirement the learning can meet, what record the school needs, how you will be assessed, and what the complete purchase includes. Compare grades or scores, recommendation dates, academic level, and duplicate restrictions. Keep unknown answers visible instead of treating an inexpensive offer as automatically usable.

Separate the type of source from its brand. A credit examination, an ACE-recommended course, an NCCRS-recommended offering, and a transcripted university course may receive different treatment at the same destination. A preparation course or voucher program can help you earn an exam result without creating another credit award.

Subscription and self-paced course providers

Sophia Learning, Study.com, and StraighterLine are important options to investigate for general education and other requirements. Course availability, assignments, assessment methods, subscriptions, and receiving-school mappings differ. Compare the exact product that includes your course rather than a general study-help membership.

Sophia describes self-paced study with a limit on active courses. Written or project work can affect how soon a course is complete. Study.com’s current college-credit support describes open-book, non-proctored finals, with course-specific work still relevant. StraighterLine’s current final Benchmark instructions require Honorlock. Check the selected course before assuming a provider meets your technology or assessment preferences.

Credit examinations and exam preparation

CLEP and DSST allow students to demonstrate subject knowledge through examinations. They can be a useful fit when you already know the material or can prepare efficiently. Your school’s exam policy determines the required result, awarded subject, and degree applicability. A published recommendation or a passing report alone does not tell you where the exam will apply.

Modern States supplies CLEP preparation and eligible exam vouchers. Its preparation should not be added as extra college credit on top of the CLEP result. Confirm current voucher, testing, and fee arrangements. Saylor Direct Credit is another route to investigate; make sure you are using its designated credit assessment rather than an ordinary completion certificate.

Look beyond the familiar subscription brands

Coopersmith and Davar offer designated NCCRS-recommended learning that may suit particular remaining subjects when the receiving school permits it. Course access, books, assignments, and proctor arrangements can differ. Search for an exact approved placement before choosing one only because its subject title looks close.

Institutional options can also be valuable. ASU Universal Learner Courses offers a process for eligible learners to complete a course and purchase ASU credit. TEL-delivered courses involve a chosen partner institution and eligibility conditions. Preserve the actual credit-granting institution in your record, and check whether you are eligible for the product being advertised.

Include learning you already have

Professional certificates, selected workplace training, military learning, prior college courses, and older exam scores may reduce new purchases. A certificate’s current recommendation does not establish that every version or every holder receives the same award. Military records also require an individual receiving-school evaluation.

Start by collecting these original records. Then find genuinely empty requirements. Buying a new introductory course is wasteful when your school has already accepted equivalent learning, while completing an attractive certificate may add little if its likely awards overlap your existing inventory.

Compare the full course basket

Make a short list of eligible options per requirement. Compare subscription duration, individual course charges, exams, proctoring, labs, records, and required university work. When a price is unverified, leave it unverified; a missing price should never win a comparison by appearing free.

Use a realistic schedule for assignments and grading. Two low-cost options can have different effects on your university start date or prerequisite sequence. Confirm the first basket with the school, buy only what you can use, and update the plan as actual completions arrive. DegreeSteps’s source directory is a discovery tool; the school-specific course plan is where applicability must be established.
